findings.severity: Low scoped dependency risk; upstream vulnerability remains OPEN
findings.audit_result: Integrator cargo-audit 0.23 exited 1 against RustSec database af7b3ec33460b8e2de8d422e16d628518891a519 dated 2026-11-12. QA read the actual report and target-specific trees; did not rerun/download advisory tooling.
findings.scope: Absent from deployed normal Wasm tree. Host path is elliptic-curve/p256 -> near-vm-runner -> near-sdk unit/dev. QA inspected near-vm-runner 0.38.1 src/logic/host.rs:2121-2185: verification consumes message/signature/public-key inputs. The local browser fixture signs Ed25519 using Node crypto, not this Rust arithmetic. No use of affected arithmetic on a cryptographic secret was identified in the reviewed application.
findings.required_disposition: Keep audit exit 1 and advisory named. Plan a supported transitive dependency upgrade before production or introducing secret-bearing affected operations. Patched >=0.7.6 is outside the current 0.5 transitive constraint; do not force a lockfile substitution without new builds and QA.
findings.limitation: No timing exploit experiment or comprehensive audit of the downloaded Sandbox/Node binaries was performed.

findings.required_disposition: Keep maintenance disclosure and include in future upstream dependency upgrade plan.

findings.scope: Present in deployed Wasm through near-sdk. The upstream maintenance warning includes known memory-leak concerns. Bounded inputs and measured receipt gas do not establish allocator correctness.
findings.required_disposition: Keep this deployed-component warning explicit. Consider a supported allocator/SDK replacement in a separately reviewed change with rebuilt hashes, storage/gas and regression evidence before production.

trust_boundaries_and_limits: This is an owner-operated local console. One session exposes all four disposable roles intentionally; role selection is not multi-user authentication. Contract authorization still validates the actual caller for every mutation.

Other local programs are trusted: they can forge HTTP Origin/Host and can reach the native privileged Sandbox RPC. Browser cross-origin restrictions, JSON-only native RPC and loopback binding protect the tested browser boundary; they do not authenticate local OS users.

Deposits are not contract-idempotent. No automatic resubmission occurs. The server blocks new deposits after an ambiguous SDK submission, and the page blocks an uncertain browser outcome; operators must resolve a transaction before creating a fresh funding intent. Do not claim universal end-to-end exactly-once deposits or recovery of an unknown browser response after an operator reload.
The final browser/source review identifies no dynamic HTML injection path. It is not a comprehensive fuzzing or hostile-RPC authenticity proof.

Prototype limits: controlled delayed physical-refund window not reproduced; callback failure can strand pending indefinitely; reviewed immutable synchronous receivers only; finite owner recovery reserve/quotas and global normal-quota availability; no operational withdrawal.
Configured request caps sum to 5120 but reachable normal requests are <=639 and total requests <=4735. Combination of all reachable maxima was not executed in this review.
No Testnet, Mainnet, real funds, paid LLM service, real autonomous LLM-agent execution, full contract-suite rerun or cold toolchain download was performed by this QA follow-up.
scope: Historical independent application review; edited extract retaining findings, limitations and public test outcomes, with internal launch and coordination metadata omitted. This is project QA, not professional audit certification.

Physical liquidity excluded from equality because protocol gas rewards can change it independently. Conservation was checked on every snapshot.
